commitResults.messageTitle: Level-0: greet the user and exit
commitResults.messageBody:
Print a greeting and a farewell, each separated by a horizontal
divider, so the program satisfies the Level-0 requirement of
greeting the user and exiting.

Extract the divider and the ASCII-art banner into named constants
so the 60-character divider literal is defined once rather than
repeated at each of its three uses.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a save-file representation to the Task hierarchy
commitResults.messageBody:
Give Task a toFileFormat() that renders the fields every task shares,
and have each subclass prepend its type letter and append its own
fields, mirroring how toString() is already built up.

Keep the save-file completion flag (getStatusFlag) separate from the
on-screen icon (getStatusIcon) so the display can be changed later
without invalidating files that have already been written.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a Storage class for reading and writing the task file
commitResults.messageBody:
Build the path from relative parts with Paths.get so it works from
whatever directory the program is run in and uses the separator the
host OS expects, rather than a hard-coded absolute path.

Treat a missing file or folder as an empty list rather than an error,
so the chatbot runs on a computer that has never run it before, and
create the folder on demand when saving.

Skip lines that do not match the expected format instead of letting a
corrupted file stop the load, reporting how many were dropped so the
user knows their list is incomplete.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-7: load tasks at startup and save on every change
commitResults.messageBody:
Read the saved tasks before the command loop starts, and rewrite the
file after any command that changes the list. "list" is excluded, so
reading the list does not rewrite the file for nothing.

Report load warnings once at startup rather than staying silent, so a
user whose save file was partly unreadable finds out before they start
adding to it. A failed save is reported too and leaves the session
running, since the in-memory list is still correct.

Ignore /data/ so a user's own task file is not committed.

Add saving to and loading from the hard disk (Level-7): a Storage
class that reads and writes ./data/milo.txt using a relative,
OS-independent path, tolerates a missing file or folder on first run,
and skips unreadable lines rather than failing the whole load.

Move every System.out / Scanner interaction out of Milo and into a
new Ui class: the banner and greeting, the divider-framed response
block, load-status and error reporting, and command reading. Milo now
talks to the user only through ui.*, never through System.out/in
directly.

Behaviour is unchanged: the fixed regression scenario produces
byte-identical output before and after this commit.

Wrap the task ArrayList in a TaskList that owns add/delete/get/size
and the numbered-lines rendering that used to be Milo's formatTasks.
Bounds checking (delete/get) now lives with the list itself rather
than being the caller's responsibility.

Milo's list-shaped helpers (parseTaskIndex, setDone, deleteTask) now
take a TaskList instead of a raw ArrayList<Task>; the number-parsing
and user-phrased error messages stay in Milo for now since they are
about interpreting user text, not about the list itself.

Behaviour is unchanged: the fixed regression scenario produces
byte-identical output before and after this commit.

Bring in Gradle build support from the SE-EDU Duke template repo:
build.gradle, the Gradle wrapper (gradlew/gradlew.bat), and the
wrapper's properties/jar. This only added files relative to where
the branch diverged (befbd32), so it merges cleanly against all the
work done since then.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add seedu-git-standard skill and AGENTS.md rule
commitResults.messageBody:
Commit messages and branch names so far followed no documented
convention beyond "explain the rationale" and "use lightweight
tags". Let's codify the SE-EDU git conventions (imperative subject
line, 50/72 character limits, what-and-why commit bodies, kebab-case
branch names, one logical change per commit) as a project skill, and
point AGENTS.md at it so future commits and branches follow it
without having to be reminded each time.

commitResults.messageTitle: Ui: import List instead of using it fully-qualified
commitResults.messageBody:
showLoadStatus() took its warnings parameter as java.util.List<String>
written out in full, instead of importing java.util.List and using
the simple name like every other type in the codebase does. The
SE-EDU coding standard being adopted in this project bans inline
fully-qualified type names in favour of an explicit import, so let's
bring this one method in line with the rest of the class.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add seedu-java-coding-standard skill and AGENTS.md rule
commitResults.messageBody:
The project had no documented Java style beyond a couple of scattered
Javadoc/simplicity notes, so consistency depended on whoever wrote
each file. Let's codify the SE-EDU intermediate Java conventions
(naming, layout, import ordering, Javadoc) as a project skill, and
point AGENTS.md at it so it gets applied automatically to code written
or reviewed here from now on, rather than needing to be restated per
change.
